mainTopic: The timing of פדיון פטר חמור and the order of preferred מצוות; the start of פרק הלוקח עובר פרתו: animals partly owned by a נכרי, and how a Jew and a נכרי acquire from each other.
overview: The amud opens by resolving a contradiction about when the מצוה to redeem a פטר חמור begins. רב ששת's answer is challenged by רמי בר חמא and set aside. רבא then explains that the two ברייתות follow רבי אליעזר, who compares the donkey to בכור אדם (thirty days), and the רבנן, who do not. A new משנה follows: if the owner will not redeem the donkey, he breaks its neck and buries it. Redemption comes first, and the משנה lists other cases where the Torah's 'if not A, then B' wording makes A the first choice. The first פרק then closes. The second פרק begins: an animal in which a נכרי has any share is exempt from בכורה, while כהנים and לוים are still obligated in the firstborn of kosher animals. The גמרא explains why the מסכת began with the donkey. It then analyzes רבי אושעיא's rule that a sale between a Jew and a נכרי is completed with money alone. אביי derives this from the word עמיתך, and the גמרא rejects other readings with קל וחומר arguments, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ששת: the thirty days only mark when one transgresses
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת resolves the contradiction between the two ברייתות. The thirty days do not delay the מצוה. They only mark the point at which delaying becomes a transgression.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The ברייתא that mentions thirty days means to say that, until then, the owner does not transgress by not having redeemed it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the earlier contradiction. The מצוה to redeem starts right away, but a person only becomes a sinner for waiting after thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות seemed to argue about when פדיון פטר חמור applies. רב ששת says both are true but are talking about different things. One ברייתא describes when the מצוה starts (immediately). The other describes when failing to do it becomes a transgression (after thirty days).

keyTerms.meaning: He transgresses regarding it (violates a prohibition by delaying)
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
Redemption

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It comes to say that he does not transgress regarding it (until thirty days).
phrases.notes: The "thirty days" in the second ברייתא is reread as the deadline for transgression, not the start of the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between two ברייתות raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two time-markers: the start of the מצוה versus the point of transgression.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree about when the מצוה of redemption begins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצוה starts immediately; the thirty days only mark when one begins to transgress.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: a ברייתא implies one should wait thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quotes a ברייתא saying the מצוה lasts thirty days, and after that one redeems or breaks the neck. He suggests this means one should actually wait the thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: "Its מצוה is throughout thirty days; from then on, either he redeems it or breaks its neck." Does this not mean it is a מצוה to hold onto it for all thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב ששת with a ברייתא. It sounds like the owner is supposed to wait thirty days, and only afterward redeem or break the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means one should wait, then the מצוה does not start immediately. That contradicts רב ששת. The proof hinges on reading "מצותו כל שלשים יום" as "its מצוה is to keep it thirty days."

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
He breaks its neck (from behind)
To keep it / to delay with it
Does it not mean...? (introducing a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama raises an objection:
Its מצוה is throughout thirty days;
from here onward —
either he redeems it or he breaks its neck.
What, is it not that it is a מצוה to keep it (waiting)
for all thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the מצוה of redemption begins immediately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא appears to say the מצוה is to wait thirty days before redeeming, so the מצוה does not start at birth.

steps.title: Defense: the thirty days are a window to redeem
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread: the thirty days are the time in which one should redeem, not a waiting period.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it is a מצוה to redeem it throughout the thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. "Its מצוה is all thirty days" means you may and should redeem anytime during those days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the thirty days from a waiting period into a deadline. That fits רב ששת: the מצוה is active from birth, and after thirty days one is late.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem it

phrases.english: No,
it is a מצוה to redeem it throughout thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִצְוָה לִפְדּוֹתוֹ כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's objection by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thirty days are a period of required waiting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thirty days are the window during which one should redeem.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא does not fit that defense
steps.stepSummary: If the thirty days were a deadline, the ברייתא should have said that afterward one "redeems or transgresses." Instead it says "redeems or breaks its neck."
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said: "From then on, either he redeems it or he transgresses."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the defense from Step 3. The ending of the ברייתא does not match the idea that thirty days is a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the defense, the important thing after thirty days is that one is now a transgressor. The ברייתא should have said so. Instead it gives the two normal options, redeem or break the neck, which sounds like the proper time to act only begins after thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It should have said

phrases.english: If so,
"From here onward
either he redeems it or he transgresses regarding it"
it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ אוֹ פּוֹדֵהוּ אוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading that the thirty days are a window or deadline for redemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording ("redeem or break the neck") does not mention transgression, which it would have if thirty days were a deadline.

steps.title: רבא: the two ברייתות follow רבי אליעזר and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops רב ששת's approach. One ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who compares פטר חמור to בכור אדם (redeemed at thirty days). The other follows the רבנן, who do not compare them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who compares them; that ברייתא follows the רבנן, who do not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the original contradiction. Each ברייתא follows a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns a היקש between redeeming a firstborn donkey and redeeming a firstborn son. A son is redeemed at thirty days ("מבן חדש תפדה"), so for רבי אליעזר the donkey is also redeemed after thirty days. The רבנן do not make this comparison, so for them the מצוה applies right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the previous approach)
It is not difficult
Compares via a היקש (textual juxtaposition)
The Sages (majority opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is a מחלוקת: according to רבי אליעזר, פטר חמור is redeemed after thirty days, like בכור אדם. According to the רבנן, it is redeemed immediately. רב ששת's approach was abandoned.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אלא tells you רב ששת's answer was rejected. Do not try to combine his answer with רבא's. רבא is starting fresh.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Eliezer, who compares (donkey redemption to a firstborn son's),
that is the Rabbis, who do not compare.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת's approach was undermined, רבא offers a different resolution of the original contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות reflect one view and must be reconciled by wording (רב ששת).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות reflect a מחלוקת: רבי אליעזר compares to בכור אדם (thirty days), the רבנן do not (immediately).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the timing of פדיון פטר חמור depends on whether one accepts the היקש to פדיון הבן.

steps.title: New משנה: if he does not redeem, he breaks its neck and buries it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that an owner who does not want to redeem the פטר חמור breaks its neck from behind and buries it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he did not want to redeem it, he breaks its neck from behind and buries it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the alternative to redemption: breaking the neck (עריפה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: עריפה is done from behind, with a hatchet at the back of the neck. Afterward the animal must be buried, because it is forbidden for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
From behind (the back of its neck)
He buries it

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he did not wish to redeem it —
he breaks its neck from behind and buries it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who will not redeem a פטר חמור performs עריפה from behind and buries the carcass.

steps.title: Redemption takes priority over breaking the neck
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that פדיה comes before עריפה, and it proves this from the פסוק "אם לא תפדה וערפתו".
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of redeeming comes before the מצוה of breaking the neck, as it says: "If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that redeeming is the preferred option. Breaking the neck is only a fallback.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes עריפה conditional ("if you do not redeem"). That shows redemption is the first choice. So although the owner may choose עריפה, it is the lesser option.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes precedence
Breaking the neck
As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: פדיה is the main מצוה for a פטר חמור. עריפה is the backup, done from behind, and the animal is then buried.

phrases.english: The מצוה of redemption
takes precedence over the מצוה of breaking the neck,
as it is stated:
"If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck" (Exodus 13:13).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by ranking the two options.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פדיה takes precedence over עריפה, derived from the conditional wording "אם לא תפדה וערפתו".

steps.title: Marrying the maidservant comes before redeeming her
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that יעידה of an אמה העבריה comes before her פדיה. Its source is the פסוק "אשר לא יעדה והפדה".
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of designating the maidservant as a wife comes before the מצוה of redeeming her. The פסוק says: "who did not designate her, then he shall let her be redeemed."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of 'which option comes first' cases. It now applies the pattern to a Jewish maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה העבריה can leave her master's service in two ways. The master or his son can marry her (יעידה), or she can be redeemed with money (פדיה). The פסוק says she is redeemed only if he 'did not designate her'. That shows יעידה is the first choice, the same way "אם לא תפדה וערפתו" showed that פדיה comes before עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation: the master (or his son) taking the Jewish maidservant as a wife
A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant
Comes first / takes precedence
"Then he shall let her be redeemed"

phrases.english: The מצוה of designation comes first
phrases.notes: Designation means marrying the Jewish maidservant to the master or his son.

phrases.english: before the מצוה of redemption,
phrases.notes: Redemption means freeing her by paying money.

phrases.english: as it is said: "who did not designate her, then he shall let her be redeemed."
phrases.notes: שמות כא:ח. Redemption is mentioned only for the case where he did not designate her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next item in the משנה's list. It follows the same model as פדיה coming before עריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an אמה העבריה, יעידה takes precedence over פדיה.

steps.title: יבום versus חליצה: the order was reversed over time
steps.stepSummary: Originally יבום came before חליצה. Now that people no longer have pure intentions, the חכמים ruled that חליצה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה. That was true at first, when people intended to do it for the sake of the מצוה. But now that they do not intend it for the sake of the מצוה, the חכמים said: the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third 'which comes first' case: יבום and חליצה. Unlike the other cases, here the order changed over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law יבום is the first choice. The פסוק brings חליצה only "if the man does not wish to take" his brother's wife. The חכמים saw that people were doing יבום for other reasons, such as her beauty or money. Once that was happening, they reversed the order so that חליצה is preferred.

keyTerms.meaning: Levirate marriage: marrying the widow of a brother who died without children
The ceremony that releases the widow from the יבום bond
For the sake of the מצוה
Originally / in earlier times

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the Torah's order itself changed. By Torah law יבום is still the first option. The reversal is a ruling of the חכמים, made because people's intentions changed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that when the Torah gives a 'first choice', that choice depends on the מצוה being done properly. If the intention is wrong, the חכמים may prefer the second option.

phrases.english: The מצוה of levirate marriage comes before the מצוה of chalitzah,
phrases.notes: Source: "ואם לא יחפץ האיש לקחת" (דברים כה:ז). חליצה is only for when he does not want to marry her.

phrases.english: originally, when people would intend it for the sake of the מצוה,
but now, when they do not intend it for the sake of the מצוה,
phrases.notes: Instead they marry her for her beauty or for money.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת יִבּוּם.
phrases.english: they said: the מצוה of chalitzah comes before the מצוה of levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the משנה's list of precedence cases and adds a reversal made by the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally יבום took precedence. Now, because people's intentions changed, חליצה takes precedence over יבום.

steps.title: The owner has first rights to redeem his consecrated animal
steps.stepSummary: When a non-kosher animal of הקדש is redeemed, the owner who consecrated it comes before anyone else. The source is "ואם לא יגאל ונמכר בערכך".
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of redemption belongs first to the owner. He comes before any other person, as it is said: "And if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to your valuation."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last 'which comes first' case. When a consecrated non-kosher animal is redeemed, the original owner gets first rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a בהמה טמאה given to הקדש. First it says the owner can redeem it, and only then says "if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold" to others. That order shows the owner has priority over any outside buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: buying back something consecrated
The owner, here the person who consecrated the animal
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
"According to your valuation": at its assessed price

steps.whatToRemember: All four cases follow one pattern. When the Torah says 'if not A, then B', A is the preferred מצוה‎: פדיה before עריפה, יעידה before פדיה, יבום before חליצה (later reversed by the חכמים), and the owner's גאולה before anyone else's.

phrases.english: The מצוה of redemption, by the owner,
phrases.notes: This refers to a non-kosher animal that was consecrated to הקדש.

phrases.english: he comes before any other person,
as it is said: "And if it is not redeemed,
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:כז. This comes right after the owner's own redemption is mentioned.

phrases.english: it shall be sold according to your valuation."
phrases.notes: The sale to others happens only if the owner does not redeem it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוַת הַגְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן הוּא קוֹדֵם לְכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the final item in the משנה's list of precedence cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner who consecrated a non-kosher animal takes precedence over all others in redeeming it.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter הלוקח עובר חמורו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first chapter of מסכת בכורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter "One who purchases the fetus of his donkey."
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional line said when a chapter is finished, and it marks the end of the chapter about פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chapter is named for its opening words, הלוקח עובר חמורו. Saying 'we will return to you' expresses the hope of learning it again. The next chapter begins a new topic: the firstborn of a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the formula said at the end of a chapter
Name of the first chapter of בכורות: "One who purchases the fetus of his donkey"

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of בכורות, on the laws of פטר חמור, is complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"One who purchases the fetus of his donkey."
phrases.notes: The chapter is named for its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This closes the chapter after the משנה's final ruling.

steps.title: Animals partly owned by a non-Jew are exempt from firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if a נכרי has a share in the animal, its firstborn is פטור מן הבכורה, based on the word "בישראל".
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew buys the unborn calf of a נכרי's cow, or sells his own unborn calf to a נכרי (even though he is not allowed to), or is a partner with a נכרי, or takes a נכרי's animal to raise, or gives his own animal to a נכרי to raise, the animal is exempt from בכורה. The פסוק says "בישראל", meaning among Jews and not among others.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. The משנה lists five cases where a נכרי has some ownership in the animal, and says all of them are exempt from בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of בכור applies only to an animal fully owned by a Jew. Even a partial share held by a נכרי removes the obligation, because the פסוק limits בכורה to "בישראל". The phrase "אף על פי שאינו רשאי" teaches that selling a large animal to a נכרי is forbidden, but once it is done, the exemption still takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus (an animal still in its mother's womb)
He is not permitted (to do this)
One who enters a partnership
Taking an animal to raise in exchange for a share of the profits
Exempt from the laws of the firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: "אף על פי שאינו רשאי" does not mean the sale fails. The sale is forbidden, but it still works, and the animal becomes exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic principle of the פרק: any ownership share held by a נכרי removes the animal from בכורה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who buys the fetus of a gentile's cow,
and one who sells [the fetus of his own cow] to him,
even though he is not permitted to do so,
phrases.notes: Selling a large animal to a נכרי is rabbinically forbidden.

phrases.english: and one who enters a partnership with him,
and one who receives [an animal] from him to raise,
and one who gives [his animal] to him to raise —
is exempt from firstborn status,
as it is stated: "In Israel,"
but not among others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן of the first פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any ownership share held by a נכרי in the animal or fetus exempts it from בכורה, based on "בישראל".

steps.title: Priests and Levites are obligated in the firstborn of kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: כהנים and לוים must still treat the firstborn of their kosher animals as a בכור. They are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים and לוים are obligated, because they were never exempted from the בכור of a kosher animal. They were exempted only from redeeming a firstborn son and from redeeming a firstborn donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule. Even though כהנים and לוים are exempt from some firstborn laws, they are not exempt from this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three separate firstborn laws: בכור בהמה טהורה, פדיון הבן, and פטר חמור. The exemption of כהנים and לוים covers only the two that involve redemption. Their kosher animals still have firstborn holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn of a kosher animal
Redemption of a firstborn son
The firstborn of a donkey, which must be redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of כהנים and לוים covers פדיון הבן and פטר חמור, but not בכור בהמה טהורה.

phrases.english: The priests and the Levites are obligated,
as they were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal,
but only from the redemption of the firstborn son
and from the firstborn donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling in the same משנה about who is obligated in בכור בהמה טהורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים are obligated in בכור בהמה טהורה. They are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why did the tractate start with the donkey instead of the cow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מסכת taught the donkey (פרק א) before the cow (this פרק), since the cow has the stronger קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the תנא first teach about the fetus of a donkey, and only afterward teach about the fetus of a cow? He should first teach about the cow, which has קדושת הגוף, and then teach about the donkey, which has only קדושת דמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the order of the whole מסכת and asks why the less holy topic (the donkey) came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור of a kosher animal is itself holy and is brought on the מזבח (קדושת הגוף). A פטר חמור's holiness is only in its value, since it is redeemed with a lamb (קדושת דמים). Normally we would expect the higher level of holiness to be taught first.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? (asking why one thing was chosen over another)
First / at the beginning
Holiness of the object itself (it cannot be redeemed)
Holiness only in its monetary value (it can be redeemed)

steps.confusionAlert: "עובר חמורו" here refers to the first פרק ("הלוקח עובר חמורו"), which the משנה above does not mention. The question is about the order of the two פרקים.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why specifically does he teach
the fetus of his donkey first,
and then teach the fetus of his cow?
Let him first teach the fetus of his cow,
as it has inherent sanctity,
and then let him teach the fetus of his donkey,
as it has sanctity of value.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא דְּתָנֵי עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the opening of the new פרק to ask about the order of the מסכת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא placed פטר חמור (קדושת דמים) before בכור בהמה טהורה (קדושת הגוף).

steps.title: First answer: the donkey is dear because of רבי חנינא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל answer that the donkey is taught first because it is beloved, as רבי חנינא taught that donkeys carried the Jews' wealth out of מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they said: If you want, say that the donkey comes first because it is dear to the תנא, as רבי חנינא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question about order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is based on how dear the topic is, not on its level of holiness. רבי חנינא taught (earlier, on 5b) that donkeys helped the Jews carry their silver and gold out of מצרים, which makes them beloved.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
If you want, say (introducing one of several possible answers)
Since it is dear to him

phrases.english: They said in the West [Eretz Yisrael]:
If you wish, say:
since it is dear to him,
in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina,
phrases.notes: Donkeys carried the Jews' gold and silver out of מצרים (5b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about order.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פטר חמור is taught first because donkeys are dear, based on רבי חנינא's teaching that they helped at יציאת מצרים.

steps.title: Second answer: the laws of a non-kosher animal are few, so they are finished first
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: there are only a few laws for a בהמה טמאה, so the תנא finishes them quickly and moves on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that since the laws of a non-kosher animal are few, the תנא finishes them and puts them aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate answer to the same question about order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is practical, not about how dear the topic is. A תנא often teaches a short topic first so he can finish it, and then spend the rest of the מסכת on the longer topic, בכור בהמה טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its matters are few
A non-kosher animal
He finishes it and sets it aside

steps.whatToRemember: The מסכת starts with פטר חמור either because donkeys are dear (רבי חנינא) or because the topic is short and gets finished first.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since the matters pertaining to it are few
of a non-kosher animal,
he completes it and sets it aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּזוּטְרָן מִילֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The laws of a בהמה טמאה are few, so the תנא finishes them first and then turns to the longer topic.

steps.title: Buying an animal from a non-Jew with money alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא rules that a sale between a Jew and a נכרי 'according to their laws' is completed by paying money, even without pulling the animal. This decides whether the firstborn is a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of ריש לקיש, quoting רבי אושעיא: A Jew who paid a non-Jew for his animal 'according to their laws' has bought it, even though he did not pull it. The animal is obligated in בכורה. A non-Jew who paid a Jew for his animal 'according to their laws' has bought it, even though he did not pull it. The animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about sales between Jews and non-Jews. It tells us when the animal changes owners, because that decides whether its firstborn is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between two Jews, money alone does not buy an animal. The buyer must pull it (משיכה). Here, when a נכרי is involved, the money alone finishes the sale. So whoever paid owns the animal when it gives birth. A Jewish owner means the firstborn is a בכור. A נכרי owner means it is exempt, which fits Step 12: an animal owned by a נכרי is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (coins)
According to their laws (exact meaning is about to be discussed)
Pulling: the normal way a buyer takes an animal or movable item
He has acquired (become the legal owner)
Obligated in the law of the firstborn

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the laws of buying and selling to the laws of בכור. The firstborn's status depends on who legally owned the mother at the moment of birth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
phrases.notes: A chain of transmission. The ruling itself comes from רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: A Jew who gave money to a non-Jew
for his animal, according to their laws,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he has acquired it,
and it is obligated in the firstborn law.
And a non-Jew who gave money to a Jew
for his animal, according to their laws,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he has acquired it,
and it is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. It builds on Step 12, where an animal owned by a נכרי is exempt from בכורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a Jew–נכרי sale done 'בדיניהם,' money alone completes the sale without משיכה. A Jewish buyer's animal is obligated in בכורה; a נכרי buyer's animal is exempt.

steps.title: Quoting the first half again to study it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the first half of רבי אושעיא's ruling so it can examine it closely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A Jew who gave money to a non-Jew according to their laws has acquired the animal even though he did not pull it, and it is obligated in בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the Jew-buying-from-a-non-Jew case again to prepare its question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. The phrase 'אמר מר' signals that the גמרא is about to pick apart a statement it just quoted. The focus will be the unclear word בדיניהם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said': the גמרא re-quotes a statement in order to analyze it

phrases.english: The Master said:
A Jew who gave money to a non-Jew according to their laws,
even though he did not pull it,
has acquired it, and it is obligated in the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the first half of Step 17 to begin analyzing it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Restates: a Jew who pays a נכרי בדיניהם acquires the animal without משיכה, and it is obligated in בכורה.

steps.title: What does 'according to their laws' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בדיניהם means. It suggests a first possibility: the laws for acquiring the non-Jew's own body, which would teach the animal case through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'according to their laws' mean? Suppose we say it means the laws of acquiring the non-Jew's own body. Then the animal case would be learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word בדיניהם refers to. It starts testing one possible answer, which it will explain in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אי נימא' means 'if you will say.' It introduces a suggestion the גמרא is checking, not a final answer. The idea: 'their laws' might mean the rules for acquiring a נכרי himself as a slave. Then a קל וחומר would carry that rule over to his animal.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for a definition)
If you will say: introduces a suggestion being tested
Of his body (the person himself)
A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'בדיניהם' means 'by non-Jewish legal custom.' The גמרא is testing a different reading here: the law for buying the נכרי's own body. Watch whether this reading survives.

phrases.english: What is 'according to their laws'?
If we say: according to the laws of his body (acquiring the non-Jew himself),
which comes through a קל וחומר:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in the statement quoted in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'בדיניהם' refer to? Which 'laws' let money alone acquire the animal?

steps.title: The קל וחומר from buying a non-Jewish slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out the proof for the suggested reading. A verse compares an עבד כנעני to land, so he is acquired with money. If even his body is bought with money, surely his property is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew acquires the non-Jew's body with money, as the verse says 'to inherit as a possession': the verse compares him to land. Just as land is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession, so too an עבד כנעני is acquired with money. His property, then, is surely acquired with money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the קל וחומר behind the suggested reading. A non-Jew's body is acquired with money, so his property should be acquired with money too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls slaves an אחוזה, and land can be bought with money. So an עבד כנעני can be bought with money. The argument: a person's own body is harder to acquire than his things. If money works for the harder case, it should surely work for his animal. This is still a proposal being tested.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To inherit as a possession' (ויקרא כה:מו), said about non-Jewish slaves
The verse compared it (a היקש: a comparison set up by the Torah)
A written deed of sale
Taking possession by acting as owner (e.g., working the land)
A non-Jewish slave
Is it not all the more so? (the end of a קל וחומר)

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוּפֵיהּ קָנֵי לֵיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: If a Jew acquires his body with money,
as it is written: 'to inherit as a possession,'
the verse compared him to a possession (land),
just as land is acquired with money
and with a document and by taking possession,
so too an עבד כנעני is acquired with money.
His property — is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם גּוּפֵיהּ קָנֵי לֵיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the קל וחומר that Step 19 mentioned, as support for the suggested reading of בדיניהם.
steps.raayaObject: The suggested reading: בדיניהם means the laws of acquiring a נכרי's body, extended to his property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'לרשת אחוזה' (ויקרא כה:מו) compares an עבד כנעני to land, so he is acquired with money. A קל וחומר then extends money-acquisition to his property.

steps.title: If the body comparison works, deed and possession should work too
steps.stepSummary: If the property of a נכרי is learned from his body, then property should also be acquired with a שטר and with חזקה, just like land and an עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with a document and with taking possession it should also work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the reading from steps 19-20. If we learn a נכרי's property from his body, the comparison goes too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד כנעני is compared to land, and land is acquired with כסף, שטר, and חזקה. So the קל וחומר should let a נכרי's movable property be acquired by all three methods, not just money. That is not the הלכה, so the argument proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — introduces a problem that follows from the previous idea
A written deed of sale
Acquiring by taking possession or using the item, like working land

phrases.english: If so,
even with a document and with taking possession it should also work!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof laid out in step 20 by showing it proves too much.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed reading of בדיניהם as the laws of acquiring the נכרי's body.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison to land would also allow a נכרי's movables to be acquired by שטר and חזקה, which is not the הלכה.

steps.title: A Jewish servant shows that body and property follow different rules
steps.stepSummary: A Jew's own body (as an עבד עברי) is acquired with money, yet his property needs משיכה. So the method for the body tells us nothing about the method for property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a Jew buying from a Jew proves it: his body is acquired with money, but his property is acquired by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stronger rejection of the קל וחומר from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Jew, the body can be bought with money, but movable property can only be bought with משיכה. So you cannot say 'if the body is bought with money, surely the property is too.' The קל וחומר breaks down, and this reading of בדיניהם falls.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore — adds a second problem
Will prove — a case that disproves a קל וחומר
Pulling the item — the normal way to acquire movable property
His body (the person himself)

steps.confusionAlert: The case of ישראל מישראל refers to an עבד עברי: a Jew who is sold as a servant. His body is bought with money, but buying his belongings still needs משיכה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, a Jew from a Jew will prove it,
for his body is acquired with money,
yet his property is acquired by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection to step 21, this time breaking the קל וחומר itself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from the body of a נכרי to his property.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A case exists (a Jew) where the body is bought with money but property is not, so the body cannot teach the property method.

steps.title: אביי: the Torah set the rule for buying from a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains בדיניהם as the laws the Torah fixed for them. The verse או קנה מיד עמיתך teaches that only from a fellow Jew is pulling used, so from a נכרי money is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'their laws' means the laws the Torah set for them: 'Or buy from the hand of your fellow' — from the hand of your fellow it is by pulling, but from the hand of a נכרי it is with money.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first reading, the גמרא brings אביי's new answer to the question of step 19: what does בדיניהם mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learns the rule straight from a verse instead of from a קל וחומר. The verse limits משיכה to עמיתך, a fellow Jew. By implication, buying from a נכרי works another way: with money.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — drops the earlier idea and offers a new one
An important אמורא who gives the new explanation
That the Torah fixed for them
Your fellow — a fellow Jew
But this — introduces the implied opposite case

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source for רבי אושעיא's ruling (step 17): a Jew acquires a נכרי's animal by paying money. That decides when the firstborn counts as a בכור.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
'their laws' that the Torah set for them,
'Or buy from the hand of your fellow' —
it is from the hand of your fellow that it is by pulling,
but from the hand of a non-Jew it is with money.
phrases.notes: An inference from the limiting word עמיתך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading rejected in steps 21-22 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What בדיניהם means in רבי אושעיא's ruling (asked in step 19).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The laws the Torah fixed for them: from a נכרי, acquisition is by money, as implied by או קנה מיד עמיתך.

steps.title: Maybe one cannot buy from a נכרי at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way to read the verse: from a נכרי there is no acquisition at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: from the hand of a נכרי — not at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's inference. Maybe the verse means that buying from a נכרי does not work in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read 'only from your fellow by pulling' as 'from a נכרי by money.' But the limit could mean something else: that from a נכרי, nothing works. The גמרא asks why we should pick אביי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: But say — suggests a different reading
Not at all, in no way

phrases.english: But say:
from the hand of a non-Jew — not at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי — כְּלָל כְּלָל לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference אביי drew in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's inference that from a נכרי acquisition is with money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limiting word עמיתך could just as well exclude a נכרי from acquisition completely.

steps.title: If his body can be bought, surely his property can
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it cannot be that nothing works, because a נכרי's body can be bought, so his property surely can be bought too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Do not think that, it is a קל וחומר — if his body can be acquired, all the more so his property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 24 with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew can buy a נכרי himself as a servant, so it is impossible that his belongings cannot be bought at all. Notice: this קל וחומר only proves that buying is possible. It does not prove which method is used, which was the flaw found in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: They said — introduces an answer
Do not think that — the idea is rejected
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Step 22 rejected a קל וחומר from body to property, and here the גמרא uses one. There is no contradiction. Step 22 rejected it for learning the METHOD (money). Here it is used only to show that acquisition is POSSIBLE at all.

phrases.english: They said: do not think that,
it is a kal vachomer —
if one acquires his body,
his property not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical קל וחומר that rules out the alternative reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse might exclude any acquisition from a נכרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a נכרי's body can be acquired, his property can certainly be acquired.

steps.title: Maybe buying from a נכרי needs two acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: from a נכרי, you need both money and pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: from the hand of a נכרי — not until there are both!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another reading of the verse to challenge אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the verse means: from a Jew, pulling alone is enough, but from a נכרי you need two acts, money and pulling together. That would also explain why עמיתך is singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Not until there are two — both acts are needed

phrases.english: But say:
from the hand of a non-Jew — not until there are two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי — עַד דְּאִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 showed that buying is possible, this challenges how many acts are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's inference that money alone works from a נכרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse might mean a נכרי's property needs a stricter process: both money and pulling.

steps.title: His body needs one act, so his property cannot need two
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a נכרי's body is acquired with one act, so it makes no sense that his property would need two.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Is it not a קל וחומר? His body with one act, and his property with two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 26 with another קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's body is the bigger thing to acquire, and it needs only one act. It is unreasonable that his lesser belongings would need a harder process with two acts. So the 'two acts' reading is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not a קל וחומר? — a rhetorical answer
With one (act of acquisition)
With two (acts of acquisition)

phrases.english: They said: is it not a kal vachomer?
His body with one,
and his property with two?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical קל וחומר about the number of acts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Buying from a נכרי might need both money and pulling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since his body needs only one act, his property cannot need two.

steps.title: Maybe either money or pulling works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a third reading: from a נכרי, either act works, money or pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: either with this or with that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more possible reading against אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 showed that only one act is needed. But maybe that one act could be either money or pulling. That would mean pulling also works from a נכרי, not only money as אביי derived.

keyTerms.meaning: Either with this or with that — either method works

phrases.english: But say:
either with this or with that,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 27's 'one act' result and asks which act it is.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that money specifically is the method for a נכרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only one act is needed, perhaps either pulling or money could be that act.

steps.title: It must match the case of עמיתך
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: the rule for a נכרי must be similar to the rule for עמיתך, which uses one fixed method.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to 'your fellow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to step 28. The next step completes the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From a fellow Jew there is one fixed method, pulling. So the parallel case of a נכרי should also have one fixed method, money, not a choice between two. The next lines spell this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to — draws a parallel between two cases

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's reading stands: from a Jew, movable property is acquired by pulling, and from a נכרי by money. The other readings (no acquisition, two acts, either act) were each pushed aside.

phrases.english: similar to 'your fellow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 28's challenge; the explanation continues next.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel structure taken from the verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From a נכרי, either money or pulling might work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Just as עמיתך has one fixed method (pulling), a נכרי has one fixed method (money).

steps.title: A non-Jew acquires with one method, just like a fellow Jew
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 29 is completed: just as עמיתך uses one fixed method, a נכרי also uses one fixed method.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'your fellow' acquires with one method, so too a non-Jew acquires with one method.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it began in step 29. This rules out the idea that a נכרי can acquire by either method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a נכרי is built to match the rule for עמיתך. A fellow Jew has one set method, not a choice of methods. So a נכרי also gets one set method, not 'either money or pulling.'

keyTerms.meaning: Your fellow, meaning a fellow Jew
With one (method of acquisition)
So too

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי acquires with exactly one method, not two together and not a choice of either.

phrases.english: Just as 'your fellow' is with one (method),
so too a non-Jew is also with one (method).

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״ בַּחֲדָא, אַף גּוֹי נָמֵי בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 29 against the 'either method' reading of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison (מה... אף) to the parallel case of עמיתך
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נכרי might acquire by either money or pulling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נכרי acquires with one fixed method, just like עמיתך.

steps.title: A non-Jew who pays for a Jew's animal acquires it without pulling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the second half of רבי אושעיא's ruling from step 17: a נכרי who pays a Jew for his animal 'according to their laws' acquires it even without pulling, and the animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: a non-Jew who gave money to a Jew for his animal, according to their laws, acquires it even though he did not pull it, and it is exempt from the firstborn rule.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא re-quotes the second half of רבי אושעיא's ruling (step 17), where a נכרי buys a Jew's animal, so that it can ask what 'their laws' means in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a Jew buying an animal from another Jew needs משיכה. Here a נכרי acquires with money alone. Once the animal belongs to a נכרי, it is no longer under the obligation of בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; introduces a quote from a teaching already mentioned
According to their laws
He pulled; the act of מְשִׁיכָה used to acquire movable items
Exempt from the obligation of the firstborn animal

steps.whyThisMatters: The practical outcome is the exemption from בכורה, which depends on exactly when ownership passes to the נכרי.

phrases.english: The Master said:
And a non-Jew who gave money to a Jew
for his animal, according to their laws,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he acquired it,
and it is exempt from the firstborn rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְגוֹי שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the analysis of the first clause (steps 18–30), the גמרא re-quotes the second clause of רבי אושעיא's ruling from step 17, about a נכרי buying from a Jew, to analyze it the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי acquires a Jew's animal with money alone, and the animal is then exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: What does 'according to their laws' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase בדיניהן refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'according to their laws' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase 'according to their laws.' This sets up the attempts to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is vague. It could mean a rule based on how a נכרי buys a Jewish person, or a rule the Torah set specifically for נכרים. The next steps test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?

phrases.english: What does 'according to their laws' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key phrase in רבי אושעיא's ruling, re-quoted in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or meaning of the phrase בדיניהן.

steps.title: First suggestion: learn it from how a non-Jew buys a Jewish person
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: 'their laws' means the laws of buying a Jew's body. A קל וחומר applies: if a נכרי buys a Jew's body with money, he can surely buy his property with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'their laws of the body,' because it comes from a קל וחומר: if a non-Jew acquires a Jew's body with money, as it says 'from the money of his purchase,' then surely he can acquire his property with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first, tentative answer, introduced with אילימא ('if you say'). This answer is about to be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מכסף מקנתו' shows that a נכרי acquires a Jewish slave with money. The suggestion argues that property is less weighty than a person. So if money works for a person, it should surely work for property.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected
His body, meaning the person himself sold as a slave
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (a fortiori)
'From the money of his purchase' (ויקרא כה:נא)
His property

phrases.english: If you say: according to their laws of the body,
because it comes from a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוּפוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָנֵי לֵיהּ בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: if he acquires the body of a Jew with money,
as it is written: 'from the money of his purchase,'
then his property, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentative: בדיניהן means the money method used to buy a Jew's body, applied to property through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Rejected: a Jew buying from a Jew proves otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר fails. A Jew buys another Jew's body with money, yet buys his property only by משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew buying from a Jew will prove it: his body is acquired with money, but his property only by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion of step 33 by pointing to a case that breaks the logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one Jew buys another Jew as an עבד עברי, money works. Yet buying that same Jew's movable property needs משיכה. So 'money works for the body' does not prove 'money works for property,' and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove; a counter-case that breaks a קל וחומר
Pulling; the act of acquiring movable items
Money as a method of acquisition

phrases.english: A Jew buying from a Jew will prove it,
for his body is acquired with money,
yet his property only by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in step 33.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole 'laws of the body' explanation of בדיניהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Buying a body with money does not show that property can be bought with money, as the case of a Jew buying from a Jew shows.

steps.title: אביי: it is the rule the Torah set for non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that בדיניהן means the method the תורה set for נכרים. The פסוק says 'to your fellow,' which implies משיכה for a fellow Jew and כסף for a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'according to their laws' means the laws the Torah set for them. 'And if you sell an item to your fellow' teaches that to your fellow it is by pulling, which implies that to a non-Jew it is with money.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first suggestion fails, אביי gives the accepted explanation of 'their laws.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah ties משיכה to 'עמיתך,' a fellow Jew. אביי reads this as a contrast: a sale to a נכרי is done with money. So 'their laws' means a Torah rule made for נכרים, not a borrowed קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after rejecting the old one
An אמורא who gives the accepted explanation here
That the Torah set out for them
'And if you sell an item' (ויקרא כה:יד)
Implying that; marks an inference from the wording

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the accepted reason why a נכרי acquires a Jew's animal with money, and so why the animal becomes exempt from בכורה once the money is paid.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
according to their laws that the Torah set for them,
'And if you sell an item to your fellow':
to your fellow, it is by pulling,
implying that to a non-Jew it is with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation of step 33 with a reading of a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בדיניהן means the Torah's own rule for נכרים: a Jew's sale to a נכרי is completed with money.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew cannot acquire at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's inference: perhaps the פסוק implies that a נכרי cannot acquire by any method.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: to a non-Jew, not at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's reading. It suggests the opposite conclusion could be drawn from 'to your fellow.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משיכה is limited to עמיתך, the פסוק might mean that a sale to a נכרי has no valid method at all. That would undo the conclusion that money works.

keyTerms.meaning: But say; proposes a different reading
Not at all, by no method whatsoever

steps.confusionAlert: This step and the ones after it follow the same pattern as steps 24–30, but the direction is reversed. Here a נכרי is buying from a Jew. The גמרא itself repeats the pattern for this new case.

phrases.english: But say: to a non-Jew, not at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference אביי drew in step 35.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Excluding a נכרי from משיכה could mean he is excluded from acquiring entirely, not that he uses money.

steps.title: If he can buy a Jew's body, surely he can buy a Jew's property
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a קל וחומר: since a נכרי can buy a Jew's body, he can certainly buy a Jew's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: is it not a קל וחומר? If he acquires his body, surely he can acquire his property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'not at all' reading with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר only shows that a נכרי can acquire property in some way, which rules out 'not at all.' The specific method, money, still comes from אביי's reading of the פסוק. In step 34 the קל וחומר failed when it tried to prove the method; here it only has to prove that acquisition is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: They said; introduces the answer
Is it not?
He acquires

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי can acquire a Jew's property, and he does it with money, based on אביי's reading of 'לעמיתך'. So the animal is exempt from בכורה once he pays.

phrases.english: They said: is it not a קל וחומר?
If he acquires his body,
then his property, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from acquiring a person to acquiring property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נכרי might be unable to acquire a Jew's property at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נכרי certainly can acquire a Jew's property, and the פסוק shows that he does so with money.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew needs both methods together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a נכרי may need both כסף and משיכה together to acquire a Jew's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: for a non-Jew, he does not acquire until there are two acts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read אביי's inference. Maybe a נכרי needs both payment and pulling before he owns the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the word עמיתך tells us that a fellow Jew uses משיכה and a נכרי uses something different. The גמרא now asks: maybe 'different' means a stricter standard, where a נכרי needs כסף plus משיכה. That would also be a valid contrast with a fellow Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. Introduces an alternative reading.
A non-Jew
Two (here: two acts of acquisition, כסף and משיכה)

phrases.english: Say: for a non-Jew,
[he does not acquire] until there are two [acts]!
phrases.notes: Two acts means both money and pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new alternative reading of the contrast that אביי drew from עמיתך.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's conclusion that a נכרי acquires by כסף alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contrast with עמיתך could just as easily mean the נכרי needs more (both acts), not a different single act.

steps.title: His body takes one method, so his property cannot need two
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר rejects the suggestion. A נכרי buys a Jew's body with one act, so he cannot need two acts for the Jew's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not a קל וחומר? His body is acquired with one act, and his property would need two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that a נכרי needs two acts by using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נכרי can buy a Jew's body (as a servant) with money alone, which is one act. A Jew's body is a weightier thing than his property. It makes no sense that the lesser thing, property, would need a stricter two-act process.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
His body (the Jew's person, sold as a servant)
His property or money

phrases.english: Is it not a kal va'chomer?
His body with one, his property with two?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: body is acquired with one act, so property cannot require two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers step 38 by ruling out the two-act reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נכרי might need both כסף and משיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נכרי cannot need more for property than for a Jew's body, which takes one act.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew can use either method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests the opposite: a נכרי may acquire with either משיכה or כסף, whichever he chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say: either with this or with that.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out 'both', the גמרא tries the other option. Maybe a נכרי can acquire with either method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נכרי could use either act, that would still contrast with a fellow Jew, who is limited to משיכה. So אביי's reading of עמיתך does not yet prove that a נכרי uses only כסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Either with this or with that (either method works)

phrases.english: And say: either with this or with that,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'two acts' is rejected, offers the opposite alternative of 'either act'.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's conclusion that a נכרי acquires specifically by כסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contrast with a fellow Jew is still satisfied if a נכרי can use either method, so כסף alone is not proven.

steps.title: The non-Jew's acquisition must match 'your fellow'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: a נכרי's acquisition must be similar to that of עמיתך, which works with one specific method.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to 'your fellow'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the 'either method' suggestion. This line sets up the reply, and the full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נכרי's rule is learned by contrast to עמיתך, so it should follow the same pattern. A fellow Jew acquires through exactly one fixed method, משיכה. So a נכרי should also have exactly one fixed method, כסף, and not a free choice between two.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, parallel to
Your fellow (a fellow Jew, from the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not finish the answer. It only states the principle ('parallel to עמיתך'). The explanation of what that parallel means comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Similar to 'your fellow';
phrases.notes: Just as the fellow Jew acquires through one set method, so too the non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the reply to the 'either method' suggestion of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallelism from the פסוק (setup; completed on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נכרי may acquire with either משיכה or כסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נכרי's acquisition follows the pattern of עמיתך: one fixed method.
